requirements.acceptance: Discover system/session inventories separately; no duplicate identity or silent adoption.
Start, graceful stop, force stop, reboot, pause/resume, autostart and delete preserve the promised disks and state.
CPU/RAM/boot edits correctly distinguish live and persistent state and required shutdown.
An adopted VM with unknown XML namespaces/device settings retains them after an unrelated edit.
An external concurrent edit invalidates the stale plan; no overwrite of newer unrelated settings.
Restricted session/backend capability is explained before mutation, not mislabeled as success.
ISO install, cloud image and existing disk creation each reach their declared verification level.
VMware OVA with supported Linux guest, multiple disks and NICs imports with correct boot/disk order.
Generic OVF/OVA fixture imports through the generic path, without pretending all appliances are supported.
Unsupported source/hardware, encrypted source and missing driver produce actionable preflight results.
Traversal, symlink, special file, XML entity, archive bomb and external backing references are rejected.
Conversion failure, low space and canceled job preserve original source and safely reconcile staging.
Registration/start/guest boot/guest reachability are reported as distinct success stages.
Multi-system OVF selection, missing source digest and source mutation between plan/apply are handled explicitly.
NAT guest has configured DNS/internet; a static target remains on its designated lab network.
A guest with internet plus two lab NICs uses only the intended normal default route.
Services-only lab permits its declared DHCP/DNS but rejects other host services and external forwarding.
Guest-only segment has no host L3/DHCP; approved guest static addressing works between guests.
IPv6/link-local/RA paths match policy; no false isolation claim from IPv4-only tests.
CIDR selection detects LAN/VPN/planned overlaps without treating the default route as universal overlap.
Existing LAN bridge works; DHCP remains externally owned unless explicitly configured otherwise.
NetworkManager bridge creation commits on confirmation and restores connectivity on timeout/crash.
Certified Netplan/networkd bridge creation and independent rollback work, including process interruption.
Ordinary Wi-Fi bridging is declined with NAT alternative; Wi-Fi NAT succeeds.
Port forwards obey bind/exposure policy, maintain stable targets and survive firewall reload/reboot.
Dual-homed paths are flagged; lab deletion blocks when external guests still reference its network.
Pool creation, disk allocation/growth/move and space accounting preserve permissions/labels and guest data.
Full clone is independent; linked clone retains declared immutable base dependencies.
Base/template deletion and garbage collection refuse any referenced or uncertain object.
Cold snapshot/revert preserves disk, configuration and required firmware/TPM identity; source branch remains safe.
Supported live disk snapshot/revert uses safe graph transitions, including injected partial failure.
Unsupported memory/TPM/live combinations fail before mutation or use explicitly approved cold capture.
Encrypted backup includes all required artifacts; restore succeeds with original VM files and app database unavailable.
Supported live backup respects consistency; shutdown/interruption produces partial status, never a valid incomplete backup.
Failed quiesce cannot leave the guest frozen; independent guardian meets the documented bound under daemon crash.
Retention/pruning honors pins, repository locks and active jobs; verification detects corrupted/missing data.
Scheduled capture obeys timezone, missed-run and credential-unavailable policy; no silent consistency downgrade.
Isolated test restore catches identity/address conflicts and reports the exact readiness verified.
USB attach/detach works live and persistently where supported, with serial and port identity behavior verified.
Identical devices, missing device, disconnect/reconnect and host-use conflict never attach the wrong device silently.
PCI/IOMMU discovery is read-only; unsupported passthrough never changes bootloader or host drivers.
Serial/SSH/viewer access and supported shares/clipboard honor opt-in and endpoint exposure rules.
Cloud-init and supported guest transports establish a non-root user/keys and report readiness truthfully.
Guest recipe runs only in approved guest context; input hash, privilege, retries and completion evidence are recorded.
Missing guest agent/network/SSH credentials produce guidance, not guessed IPs or insecure host-key bypass.
Multi-VM DAG applies successfully; second unchanged apply is a no-op with stable identities.
Cycle, duplicate identity, unknown template and address conflict fail during validation/preflight.
Mid-DAG failure can resume safely; destruction preserves external networks, retained disks and backups.
Template capture generalizes only a copy; clones receive intended identity and remain bound to immutable version.
Coordinated cold capture restores into a new namespace with correct dependencies and disclosed consistency window.
Closing either client leaves the job running; reconnect shows coherent status and ordered events.
Crash/reboot reconciles uncertain effects rather than blindly rerunning destructive steps.
Idempotency key retries yield the same operation; changed input with reused key is rejected.
Multiple clients and external changes are serialized/rechecked correctly, including resource busy conditions.
Wrong UID/socket clients and unauthorized helper actions are rejected; no generic root execution primitive exists.
Secrets and guest sensitive artifacts remain absent from default logs, telemetry and diagnostics.
Malicious paths, filenames, terminal control sequences and subprocess inputs cannot escape or inject commands.
Plugin confinement blocks undeclared files/sockets/network; sandbox unavailable fails closed.
Plan/hash/expiry/package substitution invalidates grants; a plugin cannot turn read permission into mutation.
Reference action and a second-language fixture pass handshake/schema/plan/execute/error contracts.
Simulated provider supports lifecycle/reconcile and reports unsupported capabilities without modifying core.
Malformed/duplicate-key/oversized frames, timeouts, crash and cancellation are handled safely.
Package signature/digest/path checks, upgrade/rollback and grant revocation behave as documented.
Plugin-added structured action is reachable from both CLI and TUI with the same approved operation.
Every mandatory operation has equivalent CLI/TUI behavior, validation, permission and recovery paths.
Resize, navigation, focus, cancellation and errors work in supported terminals without color-only meaning.
JSON/NDJSON are stable and clean; noninteractive commands never hang for hidden prompts.
RPM/DEB fresh install, upgrade, migrations and uninstall preserve user VMs/data and follow approved host setup.
Dependency-free core/protocol packages and sample plugin build on declared OS/architecture test targets.
User/admin/plugin docs and examples pass validation and correspond to actual command help.
Entire mandatory suite passes on the frozen support matrix; remaining issues and exclusions are explicit.
